headline: Soei preprint reports a single-developer audit of coding-agent evidence and history
summary: An Oct. 29 arXiv preprint presents Soei, a provenance and verification observability design, alongside a prototype study of 45 real VS Code Copilot agent-mode sessions from one developer. The authors report 102,233 records and 20,577 tool executions. Their audited rule-based classifier yields a bias-corrected estimate that 23.4% of code-editing episodes ended without an independent check after the last edit (95% CI 17.1–35.7); 57.8% of edit-backed to-dos marked complete had no recorded proof between the last edit and completion. The authors also report that their content-free, hash-chained ledger occupied about 20% of the raw transcript size and detected a tamper test. The private corpus is not released. These are author-reported single-user pilot findings, not population estimates or evidence that a classified check establishes correctness.
